movesets.name: Choice Item
movesets.description:
• With Trick and an immunity to status moves, Gholdengo is a dangerous Choice item attacker for offensive and stall teams alike!

  • Nasty Plot: This can be used to give Gholdengo more bite against defensive, slower teams after using Trick.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt OHKOes Pelipper and matches Make It Rain for damage against Primarina. It also stops Tera Water Garganacl from walling Gholdengo. It does make Gholdengo very vulnerable to Ground-types like Ursaluna-B and Garchomp though.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast slices through Kingambit, who otherwise walls Gholdengo, but the accuracy can be a big issue in close matches.

Other Options

  • Power Gem: Power Gem severly punishes Volcarona switch-ins, who otherwise can be very difficult to deal with. Otherwise, most Pokemon weak to Rock-type attacks will take more damage from Make It Rain.

  • Dazzling Gleam: Dazzling Gleam can be paired with Tera Fairy to crush Hydreigon, though Make It Rain deals more damage to most other Dragon-type targets like Dragonite and Garchomp.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: With this, Gholdengo outspeeds key threats such as Garchomp, Dragapult, and Hydreigon. It also outspeeds Meowscarada, but beware of Sucker Punch.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs make Gholdengo much more difficult to wall, with Assault Vest Ursaluna-B in particular being much easier to break through.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid or Modest: Gholdengo mirror matches are common enough that maximizing Speed is usually a wise idea. Choice Scarf Gholdengo particularly needs Timid to outspeed Dragapult. If using Choice Specs, Modest becomes easier to justify for cracking through Ursaluna-B more reliably.

  • 172 HP / 252 SpA / 84 Spe with Modest: This spread focuses on outspeeding Timid Ursaluna-B, Jolly Ursaluna, and Jolly Kingambit, all of whom are uncommon but very deadly to Gholdengo.

  • 212 HP / 236 Def / 52 SpA / 4 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This bulky Choice Specs spread survives Dragonite's +1 Earthquake, while outspeeding maximum Speed Modest Ursaluna-B.

  • 244 HP / 4 Def / 12 SpA / 244 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This extremely bulky spread allows Tera Flying Choice Speccs Gholdengo to survive Tera Normal Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon followed by Vacuum Wave.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Choice Gholdengo is perfectly functional without Terastallizing, it's particularly vulnerable to common Pokemon that Terastallization can solve such as Hydreigon, Garchomp, and Ursaluna-B.

  • Flying: With a Flying Tera type, Gholdengo gains an extremely useful immunity to Ground, which is especially useful on Choice Specs sets against Ursaluna-B and Garchomp.

  • Water: This Tera type gives Gholdengo a valuable resistance to Fire and Water, massively improving the matchup against Primarina and Volcarona.

  • Steel: Make It Rain becomes very powerful with a Tera boost, giving Choice Specs the chance to OHKO several Ursaluna-B variants in particular.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting saves Gholdengo from Kingambit's Sucker Punch, and can be paired with Tera Blast for a far more reliable Fighting-type attack than Focus Blast.

  • Normal: A Normal Tera type gives Gholdengo the edge against opposing Ghost-types, potentially flipping the table against hard to check sets like Trick Mimikyu.

Minor Optimizations

  • Neutral Nature and Nature Mints: Use a neutral nature Gholdengo that has a Timid or Modest Mint used on it. This way, Gholdengo can eat any Berry without being confused after Trick.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
• Nasty Plot makes Gholdengo a terror against slower teams, especially with its good bulk, unpredictable coverage, and diverse Tera Types.

  • Substitute: Substitute lets Gholdengo avoid residual damage from Garganacl's Salt Cure and eases prediction in general.

  • Focus Blast: Despite its reliability issues, Focus Blast OHKOes Kingambit, who otherwise is a great check against Gholdengo, in addition to ripping through Ursaluna-B switch-ins.

Other Options

  • Psyshock: Psyshock lets Gholdengo break through Clodsire more easily as well as OHKOing Sneasler without a boost. It often isn't particularly useful outside of stall match-ups though.

Items

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak prevents Salt Cure from chipping down Gholdengo, making it far easier for it to run Recover against Garganacl.

  • Leftovers: This is the most reliable option for keeping Gholdengo healthy and pairs especially well with Substitute.

  • Air Balloon: Air Balloon prevents Dragonite and Ursaluna-B from hitting Gholdengo particularly hard until its popped. It also ruins Breloom's chances of winning the lead war against Gholdengo and makes Hippowdon easy set-up bait.

EV Spreads

  • 156 HP / 124 SpA / 228 Spe with Modest: This spread outspeeds Adamant Dragonite, while having the same Special Attack stat as a fully invested Timid Gholdengo to disguise itself as the Choice Scarf set.

  • 84 HP / 252 SpA / 172 Spe with Timid: This outspeeds up to Modest Archaludon and Jolly Dragonite, two foes that otherwise can revenge kill Gholdengo.

  • 212 HP / 236 Def / 52 SpA / 4 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This physically bulky spread survives Dragonite's boosted Earthquake, which can be particularly helpful from stopping a Choice Band Dragonite revenge kill.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid: Maximizing Speed is useful on more offensive sets to at least speedtie with opposing Gholdengo, and outspeeding several threats close to this Speed tier, such as Dragonite.

  • 244 HP / 4 Def / 12 SpA / 244 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: Focusing on special bulk allows Tera Flying Gholdengo to survive Tera Normal Ursaluna's Blood Moon followed by Focus Blast.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Gholdengo may have a great typing, but common Pokemon such as Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Meowscarada will usually revenge kill it without Terastallization.

  • Flying: Flying Gholdengo gets the jump on dangerous offensive Ground-types like Ursaluna-B and Garchomp, as well as Pokemon that use Ground-type coverage like Dragonite.

  • Water: With this Tera type and Tera Blast, Gholdengo can severely punish Volcarona, who otherwise is very dangerous to this set.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting is a good stop to Dark-types such as Kingambit, as well as making Tera Blast into a far more reliable alternative to Focus Blast.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy stops defensive Archaludon from being able to phaze Gholdengo at all, in addition to saving it from Dark-type attacks. This comes at the cost of losing the mirror match up though, as well as being easily revenge killed by offensive Archaludon.

  • Normal: While it's a much worse defensive typing, Tera Normal does let Gholdengo surprise faster Ghost-types like Mimikyu and opposing Gholdengo, at the cost of being revenge killed by Annihilepe and faster Gallade.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
• While Gholdengo's defensive stats aren't remarkable, it's fantastic typing and immunity to status moves like Taunt make it a great defensive Pokemon, and a horrifically effective spreader of paralysis!

  • Hex versus Shadow Ball: Hex gives this Gholdengo a good offensive kick against paralyzed foes, but Shadow Ball is worth considering for its consistency.

  • Make It Rain versus Focus Blast: Make It Rain is Gholdengo's most consistent way of dealing damage to Garganacl, but this set's defensive nature makes it difficult to win the one-on-one. Focus Blast isn't nearly as reliable, but it's Gholdengo's best shot at making it past Kingambit.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet takes advantage of Gholdengo's excellent typing against physical moves, making it a good way to punish contact moves such as Outrage from Dragonite.

  • Covert Cloak: This is Gholdengo's best shot of outstalling Garganacl, since it grants an immunity to Salt Cure's effect.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is at its best with specially defensive Gholdengo, letting it withstand Ursaluna-B's Earth Power followed by Vacuum Wave without requiring Terastallization.

  • Weakness Policy: While this might seem strange on a defensive Pokemon, Weakness Policy lets Gholdengo beat opposing Gholdengo as long as they lack Choice Specs.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 220 Def / 20 Spe with Bold: The given EV spread will outspeed up to paralyzed Dragapult and paralyzed +1 Speed Jolly Dragonite.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Calm: This offers Gholdengo the best shot of surviving Ursaluna-B's Earth Power followed by Vacuum Wave after Leftovers recovery.

  • 252 HP / 84 Def / 172 Spe with Bold: The Speed investment allows Gholdengo to outspeed Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Speed-boosted Volcarona with the magic of paralysis.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Despite Gholdengo's fantastic typing, foes like Garchomp and Hydreigon are easily able to break through any Gholdengo that doesn't Terastallize.

  • Flying: Avoiding Earthquake against foes like Garchomp makes Tera Flying extremely useful for Gholdengo; this also gives it protection against Fissure from the likes of Dondozo and Garganacl.

  • Water: Tera Water is the best Fire-type resistant Tera type for Gholdengo, letting it potentially survive an assault from Volcarona and Choice Specs Primarina, though its coverage moves can still seriously damage Gholdengo.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting flips the tables on Kingambit, who otherwise only fears full paralysis, while turning Tera Blast into reliable Fighting-type coverage. It's also useful against Meowscarada, though its coverage moves can still deal serious damage to Gholdengo.

strategies.overview:
• Gholdengo has solid stats all around, most notably a high Special Attack stat, as well as an amazing typing. This means it can be used as a setup sweeper with Nasty Plot. A well-positioned Gholdengo can beat Flutter Mane, Latias, Tornadus, and Iron Crown.

  • Gholdengo appreciates Pokemon that help it set up, so good partners are redirectors like Amoonguss and Ogerpon, Fake Out users like Rillaboom and Incineroar, and Pokemon with Intimidate like Landorus-T and Incineroar, which all create free turns and increase Gholdengo's longevity.

  • Tornadus is a great partner for Gholdengo, providing speed control to better answer faster threats like Flutter Mane. Urshifu-R and Landorus are also pair well with it, since they can threaten Pokemon that resist Make It Rain like Incineroar.

  • Gholdengo loves to Terastalize to deal with common threats like Landorus, Incineroar, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao which all threaten to OHKO it otherwise. This gives Gholdengo free turns to set up Nasty Plot.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
• Make It Rain is used for powerful STAB damage, and Shadow Ball is used as Gholdengo's Ghost-type STAB move.

  • The main item used is Leftovers so Gholdengo can stay on the field for longer. Gholdengo can also opt for Metal Coat to OHKO Flutter Mane, in sacrifice of longevity.

  • The bulk investment allows Gholdengo to almost always survive a Mystic Water Tera Water-boosted Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and two Magnet-boosted Thunderclaps from Raging Bolt.

  • Gholdengo prefers Tera Fairy, but occasionally runs either Tera Steel or Dragon. Fairy allows Gholdengo to resist Urshifu-S's STAB moves and is a great defensive typing, bolstered by Gholdengo's original resistances to Steel and Poison. Tera Dragon also has great synergy with Gholdengo's Steel typing, providing welcome resistances to Ogerpon-W's STAB attacks. Tera Steel greatly increases Gholdengo's damage output and OHKOes Flutter Mane and the majority of Terastallized Pokemon, such as Tera Fairy Raging Bolt, Kingambit, and Gouging Fire.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
• Gholdengo leverages its high Special Attack stat in tandem with Choice Specs to deal devastating damage and tear through many teams.

  • Dazzling Gleam can be used as an alternative option to Make It Rain for spread damage, being more reliable and dealing sizeable damage in tandem with Tera Fairy, notably being able to threaten Urshifu-R and Raging Bolt with super effective damage. Power Gem can also be utilized to hit Fire-types that otherwise severely threaten it, namely Incineroar and Ogerpon-H, the former of which resists both of Gholdengo's STAB moves. Trick can be used to cripple bulkier foes, such as Incineroar and Amoonguss, by locking them into one move while alleviating the inflexible nature of Choice Scarf.

  • The first EV spread allows Gholdengo to live a Shadow Ball from Timid Flutter Mane or a Flare Blitz from Incineroar while having a high chance to survive Sucker Punch from Adamant Chien-Pao. The Special Attack investment with a Modest nature allows Gholdengo to pick up a 2HKO on Raging Bolt with Shadow Ball or Dazzling Gleam while OHKOing bulky Flutter Mane with either STAB move and non-Focus Sash Urshifu-S with Make It Rain. The Speed investment allows Gholdengo to outspeed Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Chi-Yu with a neutral nature under Tailwind. The second spread maximizes Gholdengo's Speed and Special Attack with a Timid nature, allowing Gholdengo to outspeed Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane that have up to 196 Speed EVs under Tailwind as well as speed tying Urshifu-R with an Adamant nature.

  • Tera Fairy bolsters the damage of Dazzling Gleam, allowing Gholdengo to OHKO Urshifu-R and 2HKO Assault Vest Raging Bolt, Landorus, and bulkless Ogerpon-W while allowing it to resist Dark-type attacks, notably Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch and Incineroar's Knock Off. Furthermore, it allows Gholdengo to take neutral damage from Fire- and Ground-type moves such as Heat Wave from Chi-Yu and Earth Power from Landorus, though Gholdengo does gain a weakness to Landorus's Sludge Bomb. Tera Steel allows Make It Rain to become extremely strong, notably OHKOing Landorus, Tornadus, and Ursaluna-B as well as 2HKOing Amoonguss, Urshifu-R, and most Rillaboom. It also drops Gholdengo's weakness to Ghost- and Dark-type attacks; however, it provides a weakness to Fighting-type moves such as Close Combat from the Urshifu formes.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Nasty Plot Gholdengo is an amazing setup sweeper thanks to its excellent defensive typing, Make It Rain, and Good as Gold, which gives it an invaluable immunity to Spore from Amoonguss and Taunt. Gholdengo has good matchups into common Restricted Pokemon such as Calyrex-I and Zamazenta-C. Nasty Plot is used to allow Gholdengo to set up and sweep opposing teams. Leftovers gives Gholdengo more longevity, while Metal Coat is used so it can OHKO Flutter Mane with unboosted Make It Rain. The Special Attack investment allows Gholdengo to always 2HKO Zamazenta-C with +2 Shadow Ball, while the defensive investment allows Gholdengo to survive Origin Pulse from Mystic Water Kyogre and Flare Blitz from Incineroar. The Speed investment allows Gholdengo to outspeed Pelipper. Tera Normal is used to give Gholdengo an immunity to threatening Ghost-type moves such as Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S and Shadow Ball from Flutter Mane, while Tera Water is used because it is a good defensive typing overall while allowing Gholdengo to resist Fire-type attacks.

Common checks to Gholdengo consist of Incineroar, Chi-Yu, Assault Vest Raging Bolt, and Calyrex-S. Chi-Yu and Calyrex-S outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo. Assault Vest Raging Bolt easily shrugs off attacks from Gholdengo, while Incineroar walls it and can hit back with super effective Knock Off and Flare Blitz. Common partners for Gholdengo include Amoonguss, Incineroar, and Ogerpon-C, which help Gholdengo defensively by aiding in its setup with redirection and Pollen Puff healing as well as Fake Out and Intimidate, respectively. Urshifu-R and Pelipper are also great partners, as they can deal with Calyrex-S, Chi-Yu, and Incineroar thanks to Pelipper's combination of Drizzle, Wide Guard, and Weather Ball and Urshifu-R's ability to outspeed and threaten all three of them with Surging Strikes. Calyrex-I and Koraidon are strong Gholdengo partners, since Gholdengo can help deal with threats such as Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C and appreciates how the two threaten Incineroar. Koraidon especially appreciates Gholdengo, as it can take on Calyrex-I + Amoonguss teams incredibly well.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Gholdengo is a strong special attacker that uses its great ability to switch into moves like Amoonguss's Spore and Incineroar's Parting Shot, allowing it to attack without being slowed down. Gholdengo is also used as a check to Pokemon like Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C, since it walls them. Trick is used to cripple support and setup Pokemon like Amoonguss and Terapagos or force Pokemon that set Trick Room such as Calyrex-I to switch out. Nasty Plot gives Gholdengo the option to set up once it has used Trick. Power Gem hits Fire-types that resist Make It Rain such as Incineroar, Chi-Yu, and Ogerpon-H. Alternatively, Dazzling Gleam threatens Pokemon like Miraidon and Koraidon. Choice Specs allows Gholdengo to use its strong Steel- and Ghost-type attacks to immediately threaten Pokemon like Calyrex-I, especially if it uses Tera Steel. The EV spread allows Gholdengo to survive Choice Specs Miraidon's Volt Switch, Incineroar's Flare Blitz, and Kyogre's Mystic Water-boosted Origin Pulse and OHKO bulky Flutter Mane sets with Shadow Ball. The Speed EVs let it outspeed the Ogerpon formes when they are at -1. Tera Steel lets Gholdengo OHKO Landorus and Tera Fairy Assault Vest Raging Bolt, and if Gholdengo is paired with speed control providers such as Tailwind Tornadus and Icy Wind Flutter Mane, it can run it to boost Make It Rain even further. Tera Dragon allows Gholdengo to resist Fire-type attacks such as Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Groudon's Heat Crash as well as Miraidon's Electro Drift and Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes. Tera Water also lets Gholdengo resist Fire- and Water-type attacks like Kyogre's Water Spout and Koraidon's Flare Blitz while not making it weak to Ice- and Fairy-type attacks such as Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash and Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

Incineroar resists Gholdengo's STAB combination while threatening it with Flare Blitz and Knock Off. Chi-Yu similarly checks Gholdengo while also outspeeding and threatening an OHKO on it with Dark Pulse or Overheat. Assault Vest Raging Bolt resists Make It Rain and avoids the 2HKO from Shadow Ball. As for teammates, Gholdengo pairs well with Terapagos, since Gholdengo walls Zamazenta-C, while Terapagos matches up well against Calyrex-S and can switch into Ghost-type attacks. Gholdengo also pairs well with Calyrex-I, since it can check Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C, which Calyrex-I struggles with. Gholdengo additionally has great synergy with Pelipper due to rain reducing Gholdengo's weakness to Fire and Pelipper threatening Fire-types that resist Make It Rain such as Incineroar and Chi-Yu. Finally, Chien-Pao and Calyrex-I are both good partners for Gholdengo, since they can threaten Raging Bolt.

strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Gholdengo works best on archetypes that can find a way to support its Make It Rain sweep. It prefers partners with Fake Out like Incineroar, Sneasler, and Rillaboom as well as redirection from Pokemon like Amoonguss and Electabuzz in order to let it set up, while Choice Specs Gholdengo pairs best with priority Tailwind setters like Talonflame, Whimsicott, and Murkrow. Dragon-types like Hydreigon and Dragapult also synergize well with Gholdengo, as they can switch into Fire-type attacks like Volcarona's Heat Wave and Incineroar's Flare Blitz, while Gholdengo switches well into the Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type attacks that threaten the aforementioned Dragon-types ands hit Fairy- and Ice-types for super effective damage.

  • Nasty Plot Gholdengo synergizes well with Pokemon like Incineroar, Rillaboom, and Amoonguss that can give it turns to set up through Fake Out and Rage Powder. Choice Specs sets prefer partners with speed control options like Tailwind Whimsicott to help them against faster threats like Dragapult.

  • Gholdengo struggles against Pokemon that resist its STAB combination like Incineroar and Kingambit. Fighting- and Ground-types like Flamigo, Sneasler, Garchomp, and Ursaluna can help against bulky Dark- and Steel-types that resist Make It Rain and Shadow Ball. Garchomp is another threat, as it outspeeds Gholdengo and threatens it before and after Terastalizing with Stomping Tantrum and Dragon Claw, respectively.

Strategy Comments

  • Gholdengo's main role is to play as a sweeper. Depending on the set, it can accomplish this either by setting up with Nasty Plot or by removing opposing Steel-resistant Pokemon and then sweeping with Choice Specs-boosted Make It Rain.

  • Gholdengo is best used as an early- or late-game threat depending on the opposing team. Gameplay should focus on either removing Pokemon that can resist Make It Rain or using Gholdengo to break a hole in the opposing team and then using another strong offensive threat like Ursaluna to clean up afterwards. Nasty Plot sets are mostly used as an early-game option to take advantage of passive leads. Choice Specs sets can be used at any point in the game due to not needing to set up.

  • Kingambit and Incineroar are Gholdengo's biggest checks, as they resist its STAB attacks and can threaten it with super effective damage. Pokemon like Sneasler, Flamigo, and Paldean Tauros-W can threaten the aforementioned checks. Another method is to focus on chipping them down throughout the game before finishing them off with Gholdengo. Both Gholdengo sets struggle with smart switches, as Make It Rain lowers Special Attack, while Shadow Ball being single target leaves Gholdengo open to the other opposing Pokemon's attacks.

movesets.name: Bulky Setup Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Gholdengo leverages its immunities and resistances from its typing and ability to set up with Nasty Plot and sweep with Make It Rain.

  • Leftovers increases Gholdengo's survivability, while Metal Coat and Life Orb allow Gholdengo to start attacking without needing a turn to setup. Metal Coat is preferred on sets that still lean on Nasty Plot, while Life Orb sets play more like a Choice Specs set that has the option to switch moves and punish passive turns with Nasty Plot.

  • Tera Dragon allows Gholdengo to resist Fire- and Water-type attacks like Flare Blitz from Incineroar and Wave Crash from Basculegion, allowing it to set up with Nasty Plot or to start attacking after getting a boost. Tera Steel Gholdengo is typically run with Life Orb to let it pick up OHKOs on Pokemon like Primarina and Amoonguss when paired with Nasty Plot.

  • The Speed investment lets Gholdengo outspeed bulky Volcarona, while the bulk investment lets it survive Wave Crash from Choice Band Basculegion-M and Tera Dark Throat Chop from Sneasler. A Modest nature lets Metal Coat Gholdengo OHKO Ursaluna-B with Make It Rain, while a Timid nature paired with 164 Speed EVs allows it to outspeed all opposing Modest Gholdengo.

  • Pros:

  • Setup Gholdengo can easily run away with the game if its given a turn to set up.

  • Setup Gholdengo can also afford to run more bulk investment, as it can increase its Special Attack.

  • Cons:

  • Requiring a turn to set up can lead to Gholdengo being OHKOed or heavily chipped before it can start doing damage.

  • Teams featuring Nasty Plot Gholdengo often have to include more support Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Electabuzz in order to get the most value out of it, as they ensure Gholdengo will have a safe chance to set up.

movesets.name: All Out Attacker
movesets.description:
• Choice Specs Gholdengo uses its high Special Attack stat, decent Speed, and powerful spread move to severely dent the opposing team.

  • Thunderbolt is a good coverage option for Gholdengo to threaten Water-types that resist Make It Rain like Pelipper. Power Gem also allows Gholdengo to threaten Incineroar while still threatening Pelipper. Trick works well with Gholdengo's immunity to Fake Out to allow it to shut down setup strategies or to force Trick Room setters like Porygon2 to switch out.

  • Tera Steel maximizes Gholdengo's damage output with Make It Rain, letting it do as much damage as possible before being knocked out and allowing it to pick up OHKOs on Pokemon such as Ursaluna-B.

  • A Timid nature lets Gholdengo outspeed Modest Glimmora and Basculegion, while a Modest nature guarantees the OHKO against bulky Annihilape with Shadow Ball.

  • Pros:

  • Choice Specs Gholdengo has a very high initial damage output, not requiring the setup turn that plagues the Nasty Plot set.

  • Teams without a bulky Pokemon that resists Make It Rain can quickly be blown away.

  • Cons:

  • Choice Specs Gholdengo's inability to switch moves and lack of setup can cause its Special Attack to quickly plummet if it tries to spam Make It Rain against Pokemon like Incineroar and Kingambit. This causes it to often have to switch out, losing momentum.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Focus Blast is an option over any damaging move for its ability to dispatch Kingambit and Heatran effectively, which would otherwise be able to stave Gholdengo's attacks off. A more offensive version of Gholdengo utilizing Nasty Plot with maximum Special Attack and Speed investment and a Timid nature serves as a potent setup sweeper and can be used on teams utilizing Sticky Web to have Gholdengo act as a hard-hitting spinblocker. Choice item sets can run an immunity ability like Well-Baked Body or Levitate to serve as a quick stopgap to Fire- and Ground-type. Psyshock is a niche option on Choice Specs sets that allows Gholdengo to 2HKO the special walls that would usually check it, like Blissey, RegenVest Swampert, and Iron Hands.

Checks and Counters

Special Walls: Common special walls like RegenVest Roaring Moon, Swampert, and Bulletproof Iron Treads can easily switch into Gholdengo and force it out.

Dark-types: Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Kingambit irritate Gholdengo with their ability to switch into it and force it out.

Fire-types and Ground-types: Gholdengo cannot nullify its weakness to both Fire- and Ground-type moves when opting for an immunity ability, causing it to be weak to one type or the other.

movesets.name: Choice Item
movesets.description:
Choice item Gholdengo acts a strong wallbreaker and speed control option, boasting a spammable STAB move and nuke in Shadow Ball and Make It Rain, respectively. Recover should exclusively be used on Choice Scarf sets to allow Gholdengo to take advantage of its good natural typing and above-average bulk, allowing it to consistently switch into offensive threats like Scream Tail, Iron Boulder, and Assault Vest Iron Crown, outspeed them, and force them out while offsetting any damage it may have taken in the process. Dazzling Gleam threatens Dark-types like Roaring Moon while still being a solid middle-ground option against Chien-Pao and Kingambit, and it is Gholdengo's strongest attack against Iron Hands. Thunderbolt is a strong coverage option that lets Gholdengo hit RegenVest Manaphy while being the best move against Kingambit. Lastly, Trick is a good option on Choice Scarf sets that allows Gholdengo to cripple would-be checks like Iron Treads, RegenVest Manaphy, and Swampert, debilitating them while opening itself and other special attacking teammates up later in the game. Adaptability is preferred on sets that only use Gholdengo's STAB moves as damaging moves, as it allows Gholdengo to feint other abilities, but Hadron Engine is preferred on sets with Dazzling Gleam or Thunderbolt to increase their damage output. Choice Specs and a Modest nature turn Gholdengo into a ferocious wallbreaker, allowing it to OHKO RegenVest Manaphy and Roaring Moon with Hadron Engine-boosted Thunderbolt and Dazzling Gleam while almost always OHKOing or 2HKOing every Pokemon in the tier that lacks a Steel-resistance or excellent special bulk. Choice Scarf instead allows it to act as a great speed control option and revenge killer, allowing it to outspeed notable threats like Zamazenta, Chien-Pao, and non-Choice Scarf Roaring Moon.

Gholdengo best fits on balance and bulky offense teams, where its capabilities of acting as either a potent wallbreaker or speed control option are much appreciated. Gholdengo struggles to break past special walls like Blissey, RegenVest Swampert, and Bulletproof Iron Treads, making physical wallbreakers that can put a dent in them like Zamazenta, Roaring Moon, and Chien-Pao good teammates; these physical wallbreakers may struggle with their inability to break past physical walls as well as their Fairy-type checks, all of which Gholdengo helps to cover, bolstering the effectiveness of using them together. Gholdengo struggles against wallbreakers that either outspeed it or survive a hit and threaten it back in return, notably Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, Kingambit, and Deoxys-S, making defensive partners like Corviknight, RegenVest Manaphy, and Roaring Moon good teammates.

movesets.name: Physically Defensive
movesets.description:
Physically defensive Gholdengo serves as an excellent spinblocker and physical wall, leveraging its great typing and useful movepool to either spread paralysis with Thunder Wave or set up with Nasty Plot and break holes in the opposing team. Dazzling Gleam dispatches Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Chien-Pao while dealing decent damage to Kingambit, while Hex is an option when used with Thunder Wave that also deals good damage to Bulletproof Iron Treads. Nasty Plot turns Gholdengo into a potent bulky wallbreaker, allowing it to potentially OHKO RegenVest Roaring Moon with Dazzling Gleam after a boost. Thunder Wave allows Gholdengo to power up Hex while slowing down threats for its offensive teammates like the Ogerpon formes, Iron Moth, and Kingambit, which appreciate their offensive checks like Roaring Moon and Zamazenta being slowed down and having the opportunity to be broken past. The given EV spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Great Tusk without Speed investment. Levitate turns Ground-types like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and the Landorus formes into setup fodder or an opportunity to spread paralysis on an incoming switch-in while also allowing Gholdengo to almost always deny Rapid Spin attempts from the aforementioned Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Fluffy turns Gholdengo into a hard-to-KO threat that can set up with ease or spread paralysis while watching most physical moves bounce off it. Well-Baked Body allows Gholdengo to check Fire-types like Moltres, Ogerpon-H, and Cinderace and turns them into setup or paralysis fodder. Colbur Berry allows Gholdengo to lure in Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Chien-Pao, OHKOing them with a boosted Dazzling Gleam or Make It Rain, while Leftovers provides Gholdengo with passive recovery that grants it with good longevity. Heavy-Duty Boots is an option on non-Levitate sets that allows them to offset entry hazard chip damage, allowing them to switch in more frequently while opening up Earth Eater as a potential ability option that punishes Ground-type moves even further.

Gholdengo fits best on bulky offense teams, where its spinblocking capabilities and general utility is much appreciated. Furthermore, bulky offense teams that can stack numerous entry hazards are where Gholdengo can truly shine as a spinblocker that can last throughout the course of a game. Thus, hazard setters like Ting-Lu, Skarmory, and Great Tusk pair well with it. Gholdengo's limit of one ability leaves it prone to Ground-types, Fire-types, or even both depending on its ability, thus, Pokemon that can switch into Ground-types frequently like Corviknight, Zapdos, and the Landorus formes make for good teammates, while Pokemon that can switch into Fire-types like Primordial Sea Zapdos as well as physically defensive Manaphy pair well with it. Gholdengo's mediocre Special Defense leaves it prone to strong special attackers like Zapdos, Thundurus-T, and opposing Gholdengo, making special walls like RegenVest Roaring Moon, Swampert, and Manaphy good partners.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Gholdengo stands out as one of the best setup attackers, with its already massive Special Attack stat and reasonable bulk bolstered further by Nasty Plot and Recover. Additionally, it provides plenty of support thanks to Good as Gold making both itself and its partner immune to status moves including Amoonguss's Spore and Incineroar's Parting Shot. Make It Rain is Gholdengo's standout move as an exceptionally high-powered spread attack, taking down the likes of Chien-Pao and Glimmora easily as well as Rillaboom at +2. Shadow Ball pressures other Ghost-types such as Sinistcha and opposing Gholdengo effectively while also hitting Steel-resistant foes such as Ogerpon-H well. Gholdengo can choose to run Recover in lieu of Protect if the rest of the team can provide the latter, making it incredibly hard to remove. As Gholdengo wants to sit on the field for as long as possible, Leftovers is the primary recovery item chosen to maximize healing; however, Sitrus Berry is a fine option for more immediate HP recovery. Gholdengo's inability to hit Incineroar for any meaningful damage make partners such as Ogerpon-W and Landorus greatly appreciated. The given bulk EVs allow Gholdengo to survive Landorus-T's Stomping Tantrum, Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch, and Heatran's Flash Fire-boosted Lava Plume. Its Speed allows it to outrun Choice Scarf Landorus-T in Tailwind. Tera Dragon is generally preferred to resist both Ogerpon-H's and Ogerpon-W's STAB moves; however, Tera Water is also fine as a good defensive typing overall.

Notable Partners

Bulky Support Pokemon: The likes of Incineroar, Amoonguss, and Indeedee-F help make Gholdengo shine, with Intimidate nullifying physical attackers almost entirely and Fake Out, Rage Powder, and Follow Me providing safe opportunities to use Nasty Plot.

Other Setup Pokemon: Swords Dance Iron Hands and Cosmic Power Deoxys-D both appreicate Good as Gold granting them an immunity to common disruption such as Will-O-Wisp, Spore, and Taunt. Deoxys-D particularly appreciates Nasty Plot in order to boost its Stored Power damage even further.

Pokemon With Immunity Abilities: Pokemon such as Heatran and Latios provide Gholdengo with Flash Fire and Levitate, respectively, making it immediately immune to types it would otherwise be weak to.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Choice Specs turns Gholdengo into a behemoth of a special attacker, with it 2HKOing bulkier Pokemon such as Indeedee-F and Dragonite with its Tera Steel-boosted Make It Rain. Choice Specs also helps turn Shadow Ball into an OHKO against the likes of Latios, Sinistcha, and bulky Gholdengo. Dazzling Gleam is one of the best coverage options for Gholdengo, allowing it to deal significant damage to the plethora of Dragon-types in the metagame such as Raging Bolt and Walking Wake. Thunderbolt and Power Gem are alternative coverage options that improve Gholdengo's chances against Volcanion and Incineroar. Trick is an option that disrupts Trick Room setters such as Porygon2 as well as setup attackers like Iron Hands. Steel is Choice Specs Gholdengo's best Tera type, as it further boosts its strongest attack while also retaining its Dragon and Fairy resistances. Choice Specs is particularly good in Partners in Crime, as it allows Gholdengo to lock into its partner's move then later break the Choice lock by having its partner switch.

Notable Partners

Tailwind Users: Whimsicott and Tornadus are Choice Specs Gholdengo's best friends, with Tailwind allowing it to deal massive damage immediately and its Good as Gold providing Whimsicott and Tornadus with a Taunt immunity. Whimsicott also offers Fake Tears to further boost Gholdengo's damage.

Setup Pokemon: Pokemon that require setup to be as threatening as possible such as Swords Dance Rillaboom appreciate the immediate bursts of damage that Gholdengo can provide.

Strong Special Attackers: Given that Gholdengo can break its Choice lock at any time by having its partner switch, a strong special attacker such as Volcanion and Landorus makes for a great partner. These also happen to pass it invaluable coverage for Fire- and Steel-types, letting it stand up to Incineroar and Heatran more easily.

movesets.name: Levitate (Chimecho / Latios / Latias)
movesets.description: Keep in mind that due to how Inheritance works, when using this set any combination of moves you wish to run must be legal on either Chimecho, Latios, or Latias.

movesets.name: Spikes + Spin (Bramblin)
movesets.description: 100 Speed EVs allows it to outspeed uninvested Gliscor

movesets.name: Fur Coat + SubPlot (Persian-Alola)
movesets.description: Maximum HP investment combined with 4 Defence EVs prevents Knock Off from Assault Vest Snorlax from ever breaking a Substitute. 100 Speed EVs allows it to outspeed uninvested Gliscor

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 3 onwards

Price Range: 14-15 points

Overview: Gholdengo's great defensive typing and ability makes it a good spinblocker that can provide great utility and offensive pressure in any given matchup. Its powerful Special Attack, strong STAB moves, access to recovery, and variety of utility options makes it an annoying Pokemon for foes to deal with when positioned well. It has access to a great number of options to answer some of its checks, including Trick and Thunder Wave. That said, Gholdengo can easily be overwhelmed by numerous powerful threats, especially since its Speed is subpar. Additionally, focusing on being more defensive hinders its offensive output, and foes can easily take advantage of its lowered Special Attack after it uses Make It Rain.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Defensive Pivot: Thanks to its great defensive typing, Gholdengo can be used as a pivot to switch into many common types of attacks. Additionally, it provides a key immunity to Fighting-type attacks, allowing it to switch in and position itself well against them.

Fast Choice Scarf User: Choice Scarf can help fix Gholdengo's Speed issue, acting as a surprise revenge option and potential cleaner with its coverage options. Gholdengo also has access to Trick, which can be used to cripple defensive switch-ins and setup sweepers.

Wallbreaker: With either Choice Specs or Nasty Plot, Gholdengo can start breaking through teams, but it has to be wary of faster revenge killers when running more offensive EVs.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Hex, Flash Cannon

Setup Moves: Nasty Plot

Utility Moves: Trick, Thunder Wave, Recover, Reflect, Light Screen, Substitute

Coverage: Dazzling Gleam, Energy Ball, Focus Blast, Power Gem, Psychic, Psyshock, Thunderbolt

Niche Moves

Memento: Memento can give your next Pokemon good setup opportunities. It can also be run alongside dual screens to maximize the sweeping potential of the Pokemon coming in after Memento is used.

Steel Beam: Steel Beam can be useful if you're looking to get more damage with Gholdengo before it faints. It functions similarly to Memento behind dual screens, utilizing Steel Beam's heavy recoil to deal heavy damage and pivot to one of your sweepers.

Endure: Endure allows for fringe strategies such as Salac Berry and Custap Berry to be effective, though it can run the risk of not working due to mistiming if your foe does not attack that turn.

Protect: Protect can snuff out attacks from the foe and can be used in conjunction with Leftovers to provide recovery. However, this risks allowing foes to have free setup opportunities.

Common Items

Colbur Berry: Colbur Berry allows Gholdengo to better survive Dark-type attacks, primarily Knock Off, and retaliate with a strong attack or Thunder Wave for Speed control.

Air Balloon: Gholdengo can safely switch in on Ground-type attacks with an Air Balloon, which gives it a free opportunity to attack, set up with Nasty Plot, or cripple the opposing Pokemon with Thunder Wave.

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf helps Gholdengo outpace faster threats that usually outspeed it and synergizes well with Trick to lock the opposing Pokemon into one move.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots lets Gholdengo remain healthy against entry hazard-stacking teams. However, this does mean that Recover becomes more vital in maintaining its longevity, and it becomes much weaker to Knock Off.

Leftovers: Leftovers provides longevity for defensive sets that don't want to rely heavily on Recover but does come at the cost of Gholdengo being affected by hazards.

Niche Items

Choice Specs: Choice Specs makes Gholdengo a strong wallbreaker; however, it can be held back due to its average Speed, not allowing it many opportunities to outspeed most threats.

Rocky Helmet: Gholdengo can utilize its numerous resistances to punish physical attackers and momentum moves like U-turn and Flip Turn.

Other Resistance Berries: Using different resistance Berries besides Colbur Berry can catch Gholdengo's checks off guard, and it can hit back with its coverage or paralyze foes with Thunder Wave.

Eject Pack: Eject Pack can synergize with Make It Rain to hit the opposing Pokemon with strong damage and switch out immediately to keep up an offensive tempo.

Eject Button: Similar to Eject Pack, Eject Button utilizes Gholdengo's defensive qualities to both tank a hit and pivot out immediately into a more favorable matchup.

Custap / Salac Berry: With Endure or simply taking enough chip damage, Gholdengo can survive any hit and use either Custap Berry to outspeed any foe once or Salac Berry to boost its speed and potentially enable a sweep with Nasty Plot.

Weakness Policy: Weakness Policy utilizes Gholdengo's bulk that allows it to survive super effective attacks and boost its Special Attack, allowing it to counter its checks and turn the tables against an opponent.

Light Clay: Light Clay is mandatory when running dual screens but can also be useful if you only rely on just one.

Tera

Gholdengo is rather situational as a Tera Captain, especially given how important maintaining its Ghost typing is for spinblocking and defensive capabilities, but it can be useful in patching up some of its weaker matchups. In certain matchups, Tera Water or Fairy can give it a better defensive typing, covering some of its weaknesses. Offensive Tera types can be used when damage output is important; Tera Steel and Ghost provide stronger STAB damage, Tera Electric boosts Thunderbolt so that it can muscle through bulky Water- and Flying-types, and Tera Fighting lets it beat Fighting-weak foes without having to rely on Focus Blast.

Draft Strategy

Gholdengo is a solid Pokemon that can fit on most teams, but it fits best on teams that rely on keeping entry hazards up and appreciate its defensive profile and offensive presence.

Entry Hazards: Prioritizing good hazard setters is key when drafting around Gholdengo. Pokemon like Hisuian Samurott, Sandy Shocks, and Glimmora can easily stack hazards, allowing it to prevent foes from removing them.

Knock Off Switch-ins: Having Knock Off switch-ins allows Gholdengo to run items other than Colbur Berry. Physically bulky teammates that can run Rocky Helmet such as Muk, Garchomp, and Landorus-T as well as Dark-resistant foes like Great Tusk and Clefable are great in this role.

Faster Pokemon: Due to Gholdengo's fairly average Speed, it's important to pair it with faster Pokemon such as Iron Valiant, Meowscarada, and Greninja to make up for that fact.

Entry Hazard Removal: Having hazard removal through teammates like Terapagos and Tentacruel ensures that Gholdengo's team does not lose the hazard war against opposing hazard stack drafts while also allowing it to stay healthy.

Knock Off Users: Having Knock Off users like Tornadus-T and Ogerpon is important to remove opposing Heavy-Duty Boots, forcing foes to take entry hazard damage while keeping hazards up via Good as Gold.

Fire-resistant Pokemon: Fire-types pressure Gholdengo easily, so having a switch-in to these attacks is necessary. Water-types such as Primarina, Rotom-W, and Blastoise as well as Dragon- and Fire-types are usually a safe bet when it comes to good Fire-type checks.

Ground-type Checks: Flying-types and Pokemon with Levitate are excellent partners to draft alongside Gholdengo so that Ground-types cannot safely spam their powerful STAB moves against it. Grass-types are also good, but keep in mind that they add more Fire-type weaknesses alongside Gholdengo.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types are able to swap into Gholdengo's Shadow Ball and threaten it with strong STAB moves, especially Knock Off. Many prevelant Dark-types such as Zarude, Greninja, and Darkrai outspeed it naturally, making it prone to being revenge killed by many teams.

Specially Defensive Walls: Specially defensive Pokemon like Muk, Heatran, and Tentacruel can give Gholdengo trouble, especially when they're able to hit back hard or set up on it. Many foes with an Assault Vest can also reliably check it.

Fast Fire-types: Fast Fire-types such as Chi-Yu, Ogerpon-H, and Gouging Fire can switch into Gholdengo's Steel-type STAB moves and pressure it in return. Cinderace especially is annoying, since it can pressure Gholdengo while working around Good as Gold with Court Change.

Ground-types: Ground-types like Ting-Lu, Great Tusk, and Garchomp are pretty bulky and dish out strong Ground-type STAB moves, often forcing Gholdengo to run Air Balloon over other important items.

movesets.name: Nasty Plot
movesets.description: Gholdengo is a fearsome setup sweeper in Ubers UU, in part due to its terrifyingly strong signature move, potent signature ability, and fantastic defensive typing. Make It Rain allows Gholdengo to output huge damage and hit important targets like Kyurem-W, Baxcalibur, and Zacian, whereas Shadow Ball offers incredible neutral coverage while hitting Mewtwo, Giratina, and Galarian Slowking extremely hard. Recover allows Gholdengo to have incredible longevity alongside its immunity to status moves. Tera Water allows Gholdengo to turn its Fire weakness into a resistance, helping against Chi-Yu and Kyurem-W, while also providing a resistance to Water, which assists against Palkia-O and Palafin. Air Balloon gives Gholdengo a temporary Ground immunity, giving it more entry points through an immunity to Spikes, Earth Power, and Earthquake from Great Tusk and Landorus. Gholdengo pairs excellently with entry hazard setters such as Magearna and Skarmory, as it blocks both Rapid Spin and Defog. It can also break through some walls with its sheer power, like Clefable and Arceus-Grass, giving teammates like Zacian an easier time cleaning up. Gholdengo struggles with faster offensive Pokemon that can halt its sweep and revenge kill it, such as Dragapult and Tera Fire Zacian, so Pokemon like Deoxys, Palafin, and Rillaboom can help Gholdengo by handing them. Pokemon with strong priority moves, like Kingambit and Palafin, can also halt its sweep and revenge kill it, so teammates like Zamazenta-C and Palkia-O, which can take Sucker Punch and Jet Punch, respectively, provide excellent support for it.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive
movesets.description: Gholdengo is an excellent setup sweeper and support Pokemon in Ubers UU, in large part due to its fantastic defensive typing, its strong ability, and Nasty Plot. Hex allows Gholdengo to do huge damage to statused foes, like sleeping Giratina and statused Arceus formes. Thunder Wave allows Gholdengo to disrupt the enemy team, power up its Hex, and cripple offensive Pokemon like Zacian, Palkia-O, and Chi-Yu. Nasty Plot turns Gholdengo from a wall into a potential sweeper with Shadow Ball, being able to boost on Pokemon that rely on status or phazing, like Arceus-Poison if its Air Balloon is intact and Clefable. Air Balloon gives Gholdengo a temporary Ground-type and Spikes immunity, allowing it to switch in on Great Tusk and Landorus easily, and keep entry hazards on the field against Great Tusk. Tera Water allows Gholdengo to resist Water- and Fire-type moves from the likes of Chi-Yu, Kyurem-W, Palkia-O, and Palafin. Gholdengo can paralyze and beat foes like Zacian and Zamazenta-C, helping teammates such as Arceus-Dark and Kyurem-W that appreciate being faster than opposing threats. However, Gholdengo struggles with Dark-types like Kingambit and Arceus-Dark, so Pokemon like Magearna and Zamazenta-C pair excellently with it. Additionally, Gholdengo has natural synergy with entry hazard setters like Magearna, Galarian Slowking, Galvantula, and Skarmory, as it blocks both Rapid Spin and Defog, making it the best Pokemon for keeping hazards on the opponent's field.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description: Gholdengo is a decent option as a Choice Scarf user and revenge killer thanks to its great offensive and defensive typing. Focus Blast allows it to hit Kingambit, Dialga, and Choice Specs Chi-Yu, whereas Thunderbolt can be used instead for Palafin and Toxapex. Trick cripples opposing Pokemon like Magearna and Dialga, which could otherwise wall Gholdengo. As Choice Scarf Gholdengo is unable to run a damage-boosting item, it sometimes lacks in damage. Tera Steel makes up for this by allowing it to OHKO Mewtwo after Stealth Rock and OHKO Great Tusk; Tera Steel also removes its weaknesses to the Dark- and Ghost-type attacks that would otherwise force it out like Sucker Punch from Kingambit, Shadow Ball from Mewtwo, and Judgment from Arceus-Dark. Tera Fighting is used exclusively on Focus Blast sets to turn Gholdengo's Sucker Punch weakness into a resistance while also allowing it to OHKO Zamazenta-C and offensive Dialga. Gholdengo is one of the most reliable forms of entry hazard control in the tier, as its immunity to both Rapid Spin and Defog allows it to keep hazards up with ease. Therefore, hazard setters like Magearna, Skarmory, and Deoxys-S make for excellent partners. Primarily used as a revenge killer, Gholdengo is excellent at enabling other premier offensive cleaners like Zacian, Ogerpon-H, and Kingambit by punching through their potential checks like Clefable and Dondozo, while also crippling Giratina with Trick. Gholdengo struggles against teams that contain strong priority users like Palafin and Kingambit, so Pokemon that can take hits from them, like Arceus-Grass, Archaludon, Toxapex, and Palkia-O are desirable partners.

movesets.name: Offensive Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Gholdengo is a good wallbreaker and glue for offense and hyper offense teams thanks to its access to Nasty Plot, its ability, Good as Gold, and its typing, which blocks entry hazard removal from Terapagos and Tornadus-T while also having useful resistances to threats such as Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. Nasty Plot allows Gholdengo to OHKO Pokemon such as Heatran and Tapu Koko at +2. Make It Rain is a powerful STAB move that can allow a boosted Gholdengo to take down Pokemon that Shadow Ball can't, such as Gliscor, offensive Garchomp, and Landorus-T, OHKOing all of them after a boost. Recover can be slotted over Make It Rain in order to increase Gholdengo’s longevity, allowing it to check threats like Iron Valiant and Tapu Lele for longer. Focus Blast is a move that complements Gholdengo’s Ghost-type STAB moves, punching holes into would-be switch-ins like Kingambit, Ting-Lu, and Heatran. Air Balloon allows Gholdengo to spinblock and threaten Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Terapagos lacking Flamethrower. Ghostium Z is a powerful option, and when used in tandem with Nasty Plot, it allows Gholdengo to OHKO specially defensive Garchomp, Moltres, and Toxapex while also OHKOing the previously mentioned Heatran without relying on the shaky accuracy of Focus Blast. Fightinium Z is another option that allows Gholdengo to bypass Focus Blast’s limited accuracy, notably OHKOing Ting-Lu and Assault Vest Melmetal after a boost.

Gholdengo acts as a valuable asset for most offensive team structures with its ability to deny hazard control while also having incredible wallbreaking potential. Pokemon such as Glimmora, Ting-Lu, and Hisuian Samurott benefit from Gholdengo’s ability to keep hazards up. Additionally, the latter two enjoy Gholdengo’s unique typing, which can help blanket check Fairy- and Fighting-type foes such as Tapu Lele and Mega Medicham. Other Pokemon that enjoy Gholdengo’s wallbreaking capabilities include Raging Bolt and Urshifu-R, as they benefit immensely from Gholdengo removing and overwhelming checks like Ferrothorn and Slowbro. Gholdengo fears Pokemon such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott; therefore, Pokemon that can reliably deal with these Dark-types, such as Great Tusk and Zamazenta, are greatly appreciated. Having Pokemon immune to Ground-type attacks is helpful against threats such as Great Tusk and Garchomp, even if Gholdengo is holding an Air Balloon. As such, Pokemon like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Moltres are outstanding partners. Moltres is an especially great teammate due to its ability to check the fearsome Fire-types in the metagame that Gholdengo struggles against, like Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona.

movesets.name: Bulky Nasty Plot
movesets.description:
Bulky Nasty Plot Gholdengo functions as a great defensive piece thanks to its amazing typing, access to reliable recovery, and its near-complete shutdown of entry hazard removal methods, as well as being a reliable offensive threat. Nasty Plot allows Gholdengo to take advantage of the foes it forces out, like Corviknight, Zamazenta lacking Crunch, and Toxapex, to enable it to break apart bulkier special walls such as Assault Vest Melmetal. Focus Blast nails otherwise-impassable Dark- and Normal-types like Ting-Lu, Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Ursaluna, preventing them from either setting up entry hazards or Pursuit trapping it. It also destroys Steel-types like specially defensive Heatran and Ferrothorn after a boost. Recover allows Gholdengo to stay healthy in the face of weak attacks from foes like Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Alomomola, letting it get more setup opportunities without fearing being chipped down. It also allows Gholdengo to check threatening Fighting-, Fairy-, and Psychic-types like Zamazenta, Tapu Lele, and Galarian Slowking throughout the game. The given EV spread allows Gholdengo to take a Choice Scarf Landorus-T's Earthquake from full health as well as outspeed defensive Landorus-T and Jolly Kingambit. Ghostium Z and Fightinium Z give Gholdengo one-time options to remove most foes in its path: Ghostium Z blasts specially defensive Toxapex and Assault Vest Tornadus-T, denying them the ability to utilize Regenerator to check Gholdengo's teammates later in the game, while Fightinium Z allows for Gholdengo to beat back its otherwise-solid answers in Ting-Lu and Blissey while ignoring Focus Blast's accuracy woes. Leftovers lets Gholdengo conserve Recover PP against the likes of Toxapex, while Air Balloon lets Gholdengo stuff Gliscor, gain setup opportunities against Landorus-T, and block Rapid Spin from Great Tusk to keep hazards on the field.

Gholdengo's great typing, which lets it deal with troublesome Fighting-, Fairy-, and Psychic-types like the aforementioned Zamazenta and Tapu Lele, as well as its amazing offensive power after a boost and its ability to block hazard removal attempts, lets it find a home on balance teams. Gholdengo greatly appreciates teammates like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, as they are able to ward off the dangerous Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott that take advantage of Gholdengo. In return, Gholdengo threatens the Poison-types like Toxapex that wall them to setup and wreak havoc, as well as checking threatening Psychic- and Fairy-types like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Hazard setters like Gliscor and Hisuian Samurott are great partners as well due to Gholdengo's near-complete dominance over most hazard control options. Both also offer unique defensive pairings with Gholdengo; Gliscor deals with Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Landorus-T by putting them on a timer with Toxic, while Hisuian Samurott takes on Fire-types like Heatran. Hazard removal options for Gholdengo like Moltres and Great Tusk allow Gholdengo to check the threats it needs to, like all-out attacking Zamazenta and Choice Specs Iron Valiant, without dealing with Spikes damage. Another good defensive partner for Gholdengo is Heatran, as it is able to put Volcarona and Moltres on a timer with Toxic while setting up Stealth Rock to chip down Gholdengo's checks like Hisuian Samurott over time.

movesets.name: Thunder Wave + Hex
movesets.description:
Gholdengo is a premier defensive piece due to its incredible ability and typing, which helps it check threats like Tapu Lele, Mega Medicham, and Zamazenta while also being immune to Great Tusk and Terapagos’s Rapid Spin and Defog from Tornadus-T and Zapdos. Focus Blast allows Gholdengo to hit would-be checks in Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Terapagos without Tera Shell. Thunder Wave allows Gholdengo to slow down Pokemon such as Terapagos, Ogerpon-W, and Heatran. Hex is boosted to new heights because of Thunder Wave, and it severely damages Gliscor. Ghostium Z allows Gholdengo to greatly harm Pokemon that are unable to be paralyzed by Thunder Wave such as Raging Bolt, Zapdos, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T. Leftovers allows Gholdengo to have an easier time switching in against Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant repeatedly. Fightinium Z helps Gholdengo secure OHKOs on Assault Vest Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Terapagos without Tera Shell while also being more reliable to hit with than Focus Blast. Air Balloon allows Gholdengo to be completely immune to Ground-type attacks from the likes of Gliscor and Great Tusk and block Rapid Spin from Great Tusk more effectively. The given EVs allow Gholdengo to outspeed uninvested Landorus-T and Jolly Kingambit while avoiding the OHKO from Choice Scarf Landorus-T.

Gholdengo fits on various playstyles where its paralysis support and incredible defensive utility are valued. Teammates that set up entry hazards like Hisuian Samurott and Ting-Lu are perfect partners for Gholdengo because of it being an effective blocker of hazard removal from Terapagos and Great Tusk, especially if it is holding Air Balloon. Wallbreakers such as Mega Medicham and Ogerpon-W benefit from Gholdengo checking revenge killers like Tornadus-T, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, and Zamazenta while also slowing down these faster threats with Thunder Wave. Gholdengo is unable to consistently break through Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Volcarona and is passive against Zapdos and Raging Bolt if it is unable to use a Z-Move. It is also easily outpaced by threats like Roaring Moon, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Charizard Y, limiting its ability to stay on the field safely. Teammates like Dragonite, Mega Tyranitar, and Zamazenta are great partners to help work around these issues. Iron Valiant is also a great partner for Gholdengo, as it appreciates Gholdengo paralyzing faster revenge killers like Tapu Lele and Tornadus-T, and in return, it takes care of Pokemon like Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit for Gholdengo.

movesets.name: Bulky Nasty Plot (Steel)
movesets.description: Boasting a Fighting immunity, the ability to deny status moves, reliable recovery, and the potential to spike the cortisol levels of any opponent, Gholdengo is a versatile and powerful Pokemon that serves as the backbone of nearly all Steel teams. With Ghostium Z and heavy investment into physical bulk, Gholdengo becomes a sturdy set up sweeper and defensive piece that has both incredible longevity and strong immediate offensive presence. Nasty Plot and Recover allow Gholdengo to find setup opportunities multiple times throughout a match, as it can setup safely in front of the many Pokemon—like Swords Dance Iron Valiant, Mega Scizor, and Sneasler—that cannot 2HKO it. Make It Rain heavily dents most Ghost-resistant and immune Pokemon, such as Roaring Moon and Porygon2. Hex and Thunder Wave can be run over Shadow Ball and Make It Rain, which allows Gholdengo to spread paralysis to the aforementioned Pokemon it checks while also crippling switch-ins like Volcarona at the cost of not being able to damage Normal-type Pokemon. When powered up by Ghostium Z, both Hex and Shadow Ball deal massive damage, nearly always OHKOing offensive Great Tusk unboosted and being similarly favored to OHKO Hisuian Samurott and most Toxapex sets after a Nasty Plot boost. Gholdengo's EVs maximize its bulk, notably allowing it to survive Mega Lopunny's Close Combat from full HP while outpacing Jolly Ursaluna and Azumarill. Spikes Skarmory and Stealth Rock Heatran are fantastic teammates for Gholdengo, as they form an entry hazard-stacking immunity core that covers Gholdengo defensively while wearing down those of its checks that must switch in multiple times such as Hisuian Goodra, Ting-Lu, and Clodsire. Skarmory handles Ground-type foes and the few Fighting-types Gholdengo cannot, such as Mega Lopunny and Great Tusk, while Heatran absorbs Fire-type moves from Volcarona and Victini. In return, Gholdengo ensures hazards stay on the field and helps Skarmory and Heatran not get overwhelmed by Fighting-types and other dangerous foes such as Superpower Ogerpon-C. Another good choice to help Gholdengo defensively is Hisuian Goodra, which shrugs off strong moves from special attackers like Choice Specs Greninja and Hydreigon. Hisuian Goodra can also use Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes, and its Dragon Tail racks up chip damage from the hazards Gholdengo stops foes from removing. Iron Treads removes hazards, threatens to OHKO foes like Landorus and Heatran that outspeed and OHKO Gholdengo, and uses Knock Off to further the efficacy of hazard-stacking cores.

movesets.name: Z-Move (Ghost)
movesets.description: Having a typing with a lot of relevant resistances, an immunity to status moves thanks to Good as Gold, and great longevity by virtue of having Recover, Gholdengo is a potent stallbreaker for Ghost teams. Shadow Ball hits most foes for neutral damage, with Never-Ending Nightmare at +2 OHKOing foes such as Mega Sableye, Galarian Slowking, and Corviknight. Make It Rain lets Gholdengo hit foes such as Alolan Muk, Mandibuzz, and Kommo-o, as well as OHKO Ice- and Fairy-type foes such as Mamoswine, Alolan Ninetales, and Iron Valiant, and at +2, this move OHKOes Gliscor, Hippowdon, and Ursaluna. The given EV spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Mamoswine and avoid a 2HKO from Mega Scizor's Knock Off, Ogerpon-C's Knock Off after Stealth Rock, and Choice Specs Tapu Lele's Thunderbolt. Mega Sableye forms a good defensive core with Gholdengo, as Mega Sableye mitigates its vulnerability to Dark- and Ghost-type foes such as Meowscarada, Greninja, and Hisuian Zoroark, while Gholdengo handles Fairy-types including Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. Sinistcha can switch into Ground-types such as Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Great Tusk that Gholdengo is vulnerable to. Fire-types such as Ceruledge and Skeledirge are solid partners that can check other Fire-types that force out Gholdengo such as Cinderace, Victini, and Volcarona.
